# [reference] Torque specifications

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Install bearings into the carrier using a spanner tool to adjust preload. [t1916]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Remove the front or rear differential cover.
2. Install bearings into the carrier using a spanner tool to adjust preload.

_Procedure reported by [t1916]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t2061] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Torquing the nut located behind the wheel.
2. [Partial] Ensuring the fastener is tightened to specification.

</details>

## Tools

- [Partial] Spanner tool (specifically for British standard pipe thread) [t1916]

## Parts

- Bearings: $20-$30 each, Toyota V6 bearings fit rear carrier [t1916]
- [Partial] Diff fluid: ~$70 worth total for both axles [t1916]

## Specifications

- **Bearing cost (rear)**: $20-$30 per piece [t1916] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **Total bearing/diff fluid estimate**: ~$70 worth total [t1916] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- Use a spanner tool to adjust preload on the rear axle because of the strange British standard pipe thread. [t1916]
- The front axle typically requires fewer additional parts than the rear. [t1916]
